headline: Mostly dry until Wednesday; wetter, more active pattern returns next weekend.
summary: A deep upper-level low offshore drifts south Wednesday, while a trough, a dip in the winds aloft, deepens over the ocean into next weekend and steers wetter systems our way. Tonight a brief ridge of high pressure keeps things mostly dry. For the next couple of days, expect fog in the early mornings. Wednesday brings spotty showers over the southern half of the region, cooler highs, and gusty east winds through the Cascade gaps. Thursday and Friday look drier. The weekend and early next week turn wetter and more active, with rising chances of flooding on the Skokomish River, which is still below flood stage. Forecasters are fairly sure about the next two days, but the weekend timing and strength remain uncertain.
changes: Since the afternoon discussion, forecasters added a possibility of gusts over 35 mph in the Cascade gaps Wednesday morning and rising flood chances on the Skokomish River early next week. The river is still below flood stage.
